chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalla', from Ayub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man marries a woman, it is not permissible for him to have intercourse with her until he gives her something worth a dirham or more, or a gift of siwiq (a measure of flour) or something else. This narration is understood as indicating recommendation (istihbab) rather than obligation (farḍ) or necessity (ijab).
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for a husband to be permitted to have intercourse with his wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar clarifies that while providing a dowry (mahr) or gift is a prerequisite for the permissibility of marital intercourse, the requirement is classified as recommended (mustahabb) rather than strictly obligatory (wajib), allowing for flexibility in the form and value of the initial payment. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that the essence of marriage is the contract itself, with the dowry serving as a right of the wife that can be deferred or fulfilled in modest forms, such as a single dirham or a gift of food like siwiq.
